mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% for two consecutive months signals wage stickiness and increased business costs, depressing near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such labor cost spikes, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both HOUST industrial production and RSAFS retail sales for two consecutive months indicates weakening overall economic demand, which precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 60-day forward return is not significantly lower than the 30-day prior average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing output (decline of at least 2%) followed within the same month by a decline in GDP deflator inflation suggests supply-side pressures, which are associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% in the current month
failure_condition: During such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 5-day prior average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month during a non-expansionary regime, the expected discount rate increase compresses the present value of future equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month and regime_hint is not 'expansionary'
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such moves are not statistically lower than during prior non-expansionary months (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE unemployment below 4.5% for the first time in three months creates a labor market tightening that elevates risk premia, resulting in a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a single month after being ≥4.5% for at least three months
failure_condition: During such episodes, 5-day forward returns are not significantly more negative than during prior periods of low unemployment (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of double-digit monthly GDP growth (>10%) in the CPIAUCSL inflation-adjusted economy creates excess optimism that is not yet fully priced into equities, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate >10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such growth do not outperform the prior 10-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp and persistent drop in both HOUST and RSAFS (each by at least 3% in the same month) indicates simultaneous weakening in industrial and retail demand, which precedes a regime shift toward supply-side bottlenecks and a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS each fall by ≥3% in the same month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, forward returns do not exceed the 30-day prior average during such dual-index drops (t-test p > 0.05).
